key_insight: A GPU-accelerated one-way Eulerian-Lagrangian framework can accurately simulate 2D incompressible turbulent flow and particle transport, with bilinear interpolation offering a strong accuracy–efficiency tradeoff.
engineering_relevance: The method provides a modular, single-GPU tool for studying tracer and inertial-particle transport in turbulence, useful for particle-laden flow analysis and coherent-structure diagnostics.
method: Extends a Fourier pseudospectral Navier–Stokes solver with passive tracer and finite-inertia particle modules.
Advances fluid fields with second-order Adams–Bashforth and particles with fourth-order Runge–Kutta.
Couples Eulerian and Lagrangian variables via bilinear, bicubic Catmull-Rom, and bicubic B-spline interpolation.
evidence_signal: The framework is validated against analytical solutions and benchmarks, and particle-number convergence plus transport statistics show bilinear interpolation is nearly indistinguishable from higher-order schemes.
watch_item: The study is one-way coupled, so particle feedback on the fluid is not modeled, which may limit applicability for dense or strongly coupled suspensions.
paper_title: A coupled Eulerian Lagrangian approach for fluid and particle dynamics
